real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to clearly visible, upright, roughly frontal dog faces where both eyes and the nose/muzzle are shown, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to clearly visible, upright, roughly frontal dog faces where both eyes and the nose/muzzle are shown, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.
parsed.evidence: Within the dog classes, activity is much higher for clearly visible faces (d +1.35), frontal views (+0.94, while side profiles are -1.33), upright heads (+0.89) and faces showing both eyes and nose (+1.23), all at the 98th–99th percentile. Coat colour and fur texture explain almost nothing (separation percentiles 42–49).
parsed.missing_data: Activity on non-dog photos with frontal faces (cats, foxes, humans) would show whether the unit is dog-specific or a general frontal-face detector, and spatial activation maps would confirm the eye/muzzle peak.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, frontal dog face with eyes and nose/muzzle all in view, framed at a moderate size; breed, coat colour and fur texture do not matter.
parsed.evidence: Clearly visible faces (d +1.35), frontal pose (+0.94 vs side profile -1.33), upright heads (+0.89 vs upside-down -1.36) and eyes plus muzzle visible (+1.23) all have separation at the 98-99th percentile, while coat colour and texture have separation near the 42nd-49th percentile. parsed.missing_data: Photos with no dog face (other animals' or human faces, non-dog classes) to test whether the unit is specific to dogs or responds to frontal mammal faces in general.

parsed.missing_data: Activity on non-dog images (other animal faces, people) and controlled rotations of the same dog face, to confirm the dog-face selectivity and the tilt preference.
